thread:
alex_support: Heads up — acme reporting a sharp p95/p99 spike ~2h ago, lots of queued requests and intermittent 504s. They say it started right after a model swap on their traffic path. sample trace id: 01F3Z7QH4. Can we triage? @jamie_oncall @ria_sre

alex_support: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-***' -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"short prompt"}' --max-time 35
# returns 504 after ~30s
```

jamie_oncall: On it. Do we have tenant id + example request payload + qps during spike?

alex_support: Tenant: acme-prod-42. Payload attached above. They reported QPS ramp from ~600 -> ~900 for ~4m, then sustained ~400 for ~20m. Errors coincide with that first ramp.

ria_sre: Looking at infra logs: admission-control hit per-tenant concurrency cap, a lot of requests were queued in front of repr-workers. p99 token latency up 5-8x. Also seeing many worker-coldstart and model-download events at same time window. Possible KV cache invalidation after model swap, causing throughput collapse.

jamie_oncall: Can we temporarily lift the tenant cap and enable a smaller fallback model to reduce tail? Current per-tenant cap = 200, backlog shows ~270 inflight queued entries. Suggest bump to 400 and enable fallback to reduce pressure.

mike_runtime: I can push a quick config bump for the dedicated pool rdx-dedicated-3 serving acme-prod-42. Action: `rdctl quota set acme-prod-42 concurrency 400` then flip fallback policy to prioritize small-quant variant. Doing now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: change applied to rdx-dedicated-3: concurrency for acme-prod-42 set to 400 (rev: 789f). Fallback policy toggled: small-quant priority.

acme_ops: Confirming — errors dropped immediately but p95 still elevated (~2.1s vs baseline 700ms). We still see queued requests and jitter.

ria_sre: Root cause hypothesis: coldstart surge + shard hotspoting. After the model swap a lot of nodes invalidated KV caches; requests concentrated on a subset of workers while others were busy warming. This reduced effective batching and increased per-request latency. Metrics: kv-miss counter spiked x12, model-downloads/sec spiked, and warmup timers show 10-30s per worker.

mike_runtime: Agreed. Short-term mitigations I recommend applying now: 1) enable stepped-warmup rollout to avoid global KV flush on swap; 2) increase fallback weight to small model for 30m; 3) raise batch_size cap modestly to let batching amortize overhead. I'll roll these flags.

deploy-bot: Applied: ff/stepped-warmup=on for acme-prod-42, batch cap increased to 1.5x on rdx-dedicated-3, fallback weight increased (ephemeral).

acme_ops: Seeing measurable improvement — p95 ~850ms, p99 ~2.6s, occasional 504s still when bursts align with model-download windows. We'll keep watching.

alex_support: Thanks — will summarize to customer. Next steps suggested: advise pre-warm for model swaps, recommend pinning model variant or reserved capacity for critical tenants, and follow up with an SRE post-mortem.

jamie_oncall: Also propose we add KV-miss and model-download spikes to alerting so we catch this earlier. @product-notify — UX note: add guidance in console for pre-warm/pin variant and an easy toggle for stepped-warmup.

product-notify: Noted — we'll add a docs snippet + console toggle for pinning and pre-warm guidance in the next sprint.

alex_support: Closing interim handoff to eng-sre for long-term fixes. I'll send the customer a remediation summary and keep open monitoring for 24h. :thumbsup:
